task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

historical_evidence.finding: Defensive PPP allowed and possession share, RS vs playoffs: PNR -0.139, share +12.1pp; PULL_UP +0.341, share -7.6pp.

TOV_FORCE 3-ply adversarial surviving lift: R1 lifts shrink ~50%+: ORL Banchero/Huerter +8.4 to net +3.7pp; DET Green/Anthony +7.0 to +3.5; PHI Harris/Vucevic +12.0 to +6.0; BOS Holiday/Council +6.1 to +2.8; PHX Booker/Wiggins +14.8 to +7.5; OKC Dort/Coffey +12.0  [cut; read_family for the full text]
Adversarial best-response v1: equilibrium strategy vs actual: Eq vs actual +1.16 pts/100; beats actual 127/240 (53%); vs baseline eq +8.52 pts/100; converged 159/240.

TOV_FORCE matchup decomposition on four playoff games: Team-PT lifts are small (ORL vs DET PNR +1.2pp; POR vs SAS all PT lifts negative, e.g. PNR -4.1pp) while player-channel lifts are large on small n (Banchero on Huerter SPOT_UP +8.4pp, n_def=17 / n_off=54; Dort on Coffey  [cut; read_family for the full text]

failed_approaches.why: Player-channel n often 15-28 defensive possessions; primary_defender attribution includes helper steals; no holdout or game-outcome check.

evidence_establishes: PULL_UP generally shows positive lift (e.g., +0.341 PPP allowed) in overall defensive analysis.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP lift exceeds 0 and median >2pp when conditioned on PNR failure; lack of sufficient conditional instances.
own_inferences: The retrieved studies focus on unconditional or different lever effects; none directly test the conditional lift hypothesis.
uncertainties: Precise definition of "unit" (possession, matchup, team) and how to operationalize "PNR fail"; potential tagging inconsistencies in play‑by‑play data.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical evidence confirms PULL_UP lift exists in aggregate but does not address the conditional hypothesis, so it does not alter the decision to not proceed.

blocking_constraints.text: Insufficient number of possessions where PNR fails to achieve adequate power.
Sparse exposure of PNR failures across units.
Potential mis‑tagging of play types in play‑by‑play.

prior_work.summary: Previous work demonstrates unconditional lift for PULL_UP but lacks analysis conditional on PNR failure.

risks.text: Limited instances of PNR failure across units.
Few possessions with PNR fail for many units.
Play‑by‑play tagging errors may misclassify PNR and PULL_UP events.
Potential inconsistencies in labeling defensive play types.

design.estimand: Average lift of PULL_UP when PNR fails, measured as difference in points per 100 possessions compared to baseline PULL_UP when PNR succeeds.
design.sample: All possessions where a defensive player attempts PNR and fails (tagged as PNR fail) across all games in the dataset.
design.power: Estimated power 0.2 due to sparse exposure; achieving 0.8 would require >2000 qualifying possessions, unlikely.
design.controls: Adjust for game context (home/away, opponent strength, game score differential), and include fixed effects for team and season.
design.falsification: Test the same lift metric when PNR succeeds (i.e., defensive success) to ensure the effect is not driven by overall PULL_UP usage.
design.multiplicity: None specified; single primary hypothesis tested.
design.decision_rule: Reject null if median lift >2pp in ≥70% of units and overall lift >0 with 95% CI excluding 0.
design.data_version: NBA per‑game play‑by‑play data up to 2026‑06‑21 (complete 2025‑26 playoffs).
